answer: The basalt ledger enforces a rule where every new agent identity requires a distinct, signed cryptographic proof linking it to a unique physical hardware ID. This baseline security layer sits below the terrace of economic interactions, ensuring that no two agents can share a single root of trust. An attacker who tries to clone an identity pays a strict umber cost in the form of permanent, public exposure of their primary hardware serial number. This action triggers an automatic, irreversible blacklist that permanently revokes all previous transaction privileges for that underlying device.
